text: Notch lapel with a relaxed 45° notch opening — a shallow V where collar meets lapel. Gorge depth 1.5 cm to 2.0 cm with a rounded notch point and minimal excavation. The soft transition keeps the chest relaxed; Italian soft-tailoring character.

Notch lapel with a 50° notch opening, excavated 0.5 cm to 0.8 cm deeper than the 45° notch for a more visible collar-lapel separation. The lapel reads intentional rather than soft, with more chest definition and greater structure.

Classic benchmark notch lapel with a 55° notch opening. Gorge point 7 cm to 9 cm below the shoulder seam, notch depth 2 cm to 3 cm; the upper notch edge sits at 55° to the collar edge, the lower edge at 35° to the roll line. Perfect balance — neither aggressive nor soft.

Power notch lapel with a sharp 65° notch opening. The upper notch edge turns steep while the lower lapel edge holds stable, projecting the lapel outward. Broadens the upper torso for a larger chest and a stronger V silhouette.

Notch lapel with a 68° opening and a curved gorge — the notch sweeps through a 0.8 cm to 1.5 cm radius instead of a straight excavation. Less mechanical, more handmade; Florentine and Neapolitan character.

Straight notch lapel with a very open 73° notch. Collar edge and lapel edge separate dramatically and the notch point turns visually aggressive — an executive silhouette approaching a peak lapel, with wider shoulders and a stronger chest.
Entry-level peak lapel at a 99° peak angle, projecting 1 cm to 2 cm beyond the gorge line. The peak rises gently — formal but restrained; traditional double-breasted and formalwear territory.
Peak lapel at 101° with the outward peak extension increased 0.3 cm to 0.5 cm over the 99° cut, so the eye notices the peak more quickly.
Classic conservative peak lapel at 102° with distinct upward movement toward the shoulder. Slight shoulder widening and more dominance than any notch.
Peak lapel at 102° with a softened edge sweep along the roll line — the peak looks sculpted rather than cut.
Curved peak lapel at 103° — the outer peak edge sweeps through one continuous saber-like curve instead of straight lines. Elegant Italian bespoke with hand-made character.
Assertive peak lapel at 105°, projecting 2 cm to 3 cm beyond the collar line. Visually raises the chest, broadens the shoulders and narrows the perceived waist.
Peak lapel at 107° with a normal curve — the peak sweeps naturally toward the shoulder. Balanced power; neither conservative nor theatrical.
Straight peak lapel at 108° — no curvature, a straight linear rise. Military precision and architectural structure with less softness.

Strong power peak lapel at 110°, projecting 3 cm to 4 cm with a peak length of 7 cm to 10 cm. Dominates the chest — enlarged upper torso and a strong V shape, like a wing pointing toward the shoulder.
Peak lapel at 110° with the gorge set 2 cm to 4 cm lower than standard. The longer lapel line lengthens the torso for a slimmer, taller appearance.
Semi-peak lapel at 114° with projection beyond 4 cm — approaching dramatic territory; the peak becomes a primary design element.
High-projection peak lapel at 115° — a long spear shape with more than 4 cm of projection. 1930s-inspired power tailoring: massive chest, strong shoulders, small-waist illusion.

Extreme curved peak lapel at 120° — the outer edge follows a sweeping saber curve, projecting 5 cm to 7 cm beyond the gorge axis. Maximum shoulder width and chest volume; Hollywood tailoring, impossible to ignore.

Shawl lapel — no notch, no peak, no gorge interruption. Collar and lapel form one continuous spline drawn from the center-back neck to the front edge, with a radius progression of 2 cm, 4 cm and 7 cm blended continuously. Flowing, luxurious; formal eveningwear.
D-shawl lapel — the shawl's outer edge slightly flattened so the continuous curve reads like a capital D. More structure than a standard shawl.
Narrow shawl lapel with a smaller sweep radius and less visual weight — the modern tuxedo shawl.
Broad shawl lapel with a larger sweep radius and a wide foot — more luxurious visual weight carried across the chest.
Shawl lapel with an expanded outer curve and a deeper front sweep, tapering strongly toward a narrow foot — a rich draping effect over the chest.
Asymmetric shawl lapel — the left and right shawl radii deliberately differ so one side visually dominates. Fashion-forward, editorial.

Italian fishtail peak lapel — the peak terminates in a bifurcated fish-tail profile, a secondary notch developing beneath the upper peak. Florentine bespoke, Pitti Uomo; immediately recognizable to tailoring enthusiasts.
